chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washa from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayer is withheld for forty days, and if he dies during the forty days, he dies the death of ignorance; and if he repents, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, repents towards him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer and spiritual status for one who drinks an intoxicant in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the spiritual consequence of consuming intoxicants, specifically the withholding of prayer for forty days, a period often associated with the completion of a minor cycle of spiritual purification in Shia jurisprudence. The designation of 'death of ignorance' (mitat jahiliyyah) for those who die within this window underscores a state of spiritual negligence, yet the promise of divine forgiveness upon repentance highlights the balance between justice and mercy in Shia theological tradition.
